change.before: "SHA-256 always used when signing with RSA"
change.after: "3072-bit keys use SHA-384, 4096-bit keys use SHA-512"

original.statement: From v1.17.0 cert-manager picks the RSA signing hash by key length (3072-bit uses SHA-384, 4096-bit uses SHA-512) instead of always using SHA-256.

decision.reason: The release-notes section [ev-c76ce5c9366c] (Major Themes › RSA Certificate Compliance; its full text appears in the change text) says cert-manager previously always used SHA-256 when signing with RSA. In v1.17.0 it picks the hash from the RSA key length: SHA-384 for 3072-bit keys and SHA-512 for 4096-bit keys. That is the same configuration with different semantics, so behavior-changed with these before/after values is right, and rsa-signature-hash-algorithm is a short kebab-case name from the evidence's own words. Confidence is low because the shown excerpt is cut off before the sentences about the hash algorithm.
